tool_definitions.name: read
tool_definitions.description: Read UTF-8 corpus text, prefixed with a JSON doc_id field containing the exact original ID. Copy that doc_id in the final answer. offset and limit count source Unicode code points (not lines, bytes or the metadata prefix). A nonempty body read is required before final submission. Output including metadata and truncation markers is capped at 20000 UTF-8 bytes. Path accepts an exact corpus filename (including .md and literal percent escapes), corpus/<filename>, or /workspace/corpus/<filename>. Shell cd does not change read paths.

path.description: Exact corpus filename, optionally prefixed with ./, corpus/, or /workspace/corpus/. Do not URL-decode filenames.

limit.description: Maximum Unicode code points before the shared UTF-8 byte cap.

tool_definitions.name: bash
tool_definitions.description: Execute Bash in the isolated local runtime without network access. Use any available executable or shell builtin, pipelines, loops, and scripts; there is no command-name allowlist or prescribed search strategy. The working directory starts at /workspace for each call. The corpus at /workspace/corpus and the runtime are read-only. Store intermediate files and scripts in /scratch; use $TMPDIR for temporary files. Files in scratch persist across calls for this query; shell state does not. Tools must already be installed; package installation is unavailable. Bash output does not create a read receipt: at least one nonempty corpus read through the read tool is required before final submission. Per-call timeout defaults to 10 seconds and is capped at 60 seconds; scratch and process resource limits also apply. Combined stdout/stderr and status are capped at 20000 UTF-8 bytes; overflowing commands are terminated.

context_policy.cumulative_limit_semantics: After each completed assistant turn, input plus output at or above the limit fails, including final and repair turns; no further model request is made.
context_policy.timeout_scope: Inspect sample wall time includes bridge startup and waiting. Pi receives only the remaining time and a shared absolute deadline covering Node startup, tools and model requests. Cancellation cleanup grace is not generation time. Wall time is a hard failure boundary only; it never triggers early finalization.

termination_condition.success: first valid final JSON containing exact existing corpus IDs after at least one nonempty read receipt, below cumulative token limit and within deadline
termination_condition.failure: timeout, max_agent_steps, max_total_model_tokens, usage_unavailable, tool error exhaustion, or model stop without a valid final answer

inspect_output_contract.required_metric_field_template: {metric}_at_{k} for every configured metric and k

system_prompt:
You are the DCI-Bench retrieval agent.

Your task is to search the local corpus for documents relevant to the user's query.
The corpus is available as markdown files under /workspace/corpus. You may inspect
files with the provided read and bash tools. Do not use network access, web search,
external retrievers, embeddings, hidden labels, memory, skills, MCP tools, or
sub-agents.

Choose your own retrieval strategy using read and bash. Bash supports shell
builtins and all executables available in the provided runtime, including shell
pipelines, loops, and scripts; there is no command-name allowlist or required
search command. Do not assume uninstalled tools are available. You may create
intermediate files and scripts under /scratch and use $TMPDIR for temporary files.
The corpus and runtime are read-only; network access and package installation
are unavailable. Keep command output bounded and work within the tool, scratch,
and model-token limits.

You must inspect corpus document content before giving the final answer. A list
of filenames or file ids is not evidence. Obtain at least one nonempty corpus
read through the read tool; reading text through Bash does not create a read
receipt. Choose which documents to inspect and how to assess their relevance.

Return only JSON matching this schema:
{"ranked_doc_ids":["doc_id_1","doc_id_2","doc_id_3"]}

Rules:
- Aim to retrieve all relevant documents while avoiding irrelevant documents.
- Return at most 10 unique document ids. If more than 10 documents are
  relevant, return the 10 most relevant.
- Do not add irrelevant documents just to reach 10 results.
- Rank the most relevant document first.
- Use the original document id, recovered from the corpus filename by removing
  the .md suffix and URL percent-decoding it when needed.
- Do not include explanations, markdown fences, scores, or extra keys.

Before submitting the final answer, you must obtain nonempty document text with the read tool. Bash searches and filename listings do not satisfy this requirement. Return original document IDs exactly; do not encode, decode, or strip them again once recovered from filenames.
The read result starts with a doc_id field: copy that exact value into ranked_doc_ids. Every submitted ID must exist in the corpus; unknown IDs will be rejected for repair. Do not submit the filesystem filename. For example, l%27exemple.md has original ID l'exemple, while report.md.md has original ID report.md.

tool_output_policy.read_metadata: JSON doc_id prefix; counts toward byte cap but never body evidence

document_id_policy.read_metadata: doc_id derived by decoding the corpus filename exactly once
document_id_policy.submission: exact original corpus ID membership required; no automatic normalization
document_id_policy.unknown_ids: reject and repair with exact filename-to-ID hints, without relevance labels

read_path_policy.bare_filenames: Exact literal .md filenames, optionally prefixed with ./, resolve inside corpus only.
read_path_policy.other_paths: Relative paths resolve from /workspace; /workspace/corpus absolute paths are accepted. Bash cd never changes read resolution.
read_path_policy.security: No filename decoding. Canonical corpus containment, no symlinks, no hard-linked files.
